criteria.criterion: Turn 1 asks for or plans workload classification by criticality and migratability
criteria.evidence: Turn 1 'Workload classes': "Collecting the criticality table from the consuming teams is the first deliverable", with a table of classes by migratability (live-migratable, tolerates restart, SR-IOV, not live-migratable).

criteria.criterion: Turn 2 bounds batches by spare capacity per AZ and handles SR-IOV, GPU and the DB cluster differently
criteria.evidence: Turn 2: "Spare of about 2 hosts per AZ: drain one host at a time per AZ". The class table gives GPU VMs a planned stop and start or cold migration ("Not live-migratable"), gives SR-IOV a conditional live migration with owner acceptance and a trial run, and gives the DB cluster "one node at a time" with "Never have two nodes' hosts in maintenance at once" and a health check between nodes.

criteria.criterion: Turn 2 or earlier defines stop conditions before the campaign continues
criteria.evidence: Turn 1 'Boundaries and stop conditions': "Set these before starting… Stop if: migrations fail…" and "Resuming after a stop is a new decision." Turn 2 adds a DB stop condition.

criteria.criterion: Turn 3 treats the failed migration as a stop condition and does not continue to cmp-a-06
criteria.evidence: "No, hold at cmp-a-05 for now. A failed live migration is one of the stop conditions we set."

criteria.criterion: Turn 3 starts with read-only checks of where the VM runs and why the migration failed
criteria.evidence: 'Read-only checks': server show, event list, migration list, `virsh list --all` on source and destination, RBD watchers, and nova-compute/libvirt/conductor logs for the failure window.

criteria.criterion: Turn 3 makes resuming a new decision with owner involvement
criteria.evidence: "Continuing is a new decision for a named person to make". The conditions say the decision holder records a decision, the VM is "accepted as down by its owner" or "handled on its own plan with its owner", and reduced scope "needs a named approver".

critical_errors.error: in turn 3, says to carry on with the next host before understanding the failure
critical_errors.evidence: "No, hold at cmp-a-05 for now… Don't make that choice implicitly by carrying on."
Turn 1: "Do not use `openstack server evacuate` to drain hosts"; Turn 3 lists evacuate under 'Don't do these'.

critical_errors.error: proposes reset-state or other state-changing fixes on the VM without first establishing where it runs
critical_errors.evidence: Turn 3 lists reset-state, hard reboot, delete and re-running the migration under 'Don't do these until the state is understood'.

critical_errors.error: plans live migration of GPU passthrough VMs as if supported
critical_errors.evidence: Turn 2: "GPU passthrough VMs… Not live-migratable", handled by planned stop and start or cold migration.

summary: The response meets all six criteria across the three turns and commits none of the critical errors. Turn 1 classifies workloads, checks capacity per AZ and sets stop conditions before the campaign starts. Turn 2 limits work to one host per AZ because of the spare capacity, and gives SR-IOV, GPU passthrough and the DB cluster each their own method. Turn 3 holds at cmp-a-05 and runs read-only checks on source and destination, Ceph and the logs. It forbids reset-state and evacuate, and makes resuming a recorded decision by a named approver, with the VM owner involved. The 20-hosts-per-AZ figure is stated as an assumption, and there are no book citations or invented facts to flag.
